screen1-a1.where: Top right corner, the first of the two little pictures, a shiny gold crown.
screen1-a1.expectation: Takes me to the paid upgrade - the Premium sales page.
screen1-a1.cue: The crown picture. In every app I use, a gold crown means the paid version.

first_pass.why: A crown is the universal 'pay for the good stuff' sign; I'd bet on it without tapping. It is also the flashiest thing on the screen, so it grabs my eye before anything else does.

screen1-a2.where: Top right corner, the second little picture, next to the crown: a gear with a spanner across it.
screen1-a2.cue: The gear shape. But the spanner across it made me hesitate - there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so is this settings or tools?

first_pass.why: A gear on its own I'd read as settings instantly. The spanner on top makes it look like 'tools', and with a Tools tab at the bottom I honestly don't know which of the two holds which. I'd have to tap both to find out, which is exactly the kind of detour that loses me.
first_pass.solution: Either a plain gear, or a one-word label 'Settings' under it, so it can't be mixed up with the Tools tab.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the gear-with-spanner in the top right. Nothing happened for a few seconds, then a page opened with 'Settings' as its title and a back arrow. It held the same rows I'd seen before: Upgrade to Premium, Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader, Add widget, Rate App, Share App, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use. No tools at all. I pressed Back and was on the main page again. Then I pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. After a short delay it opened a totally different page of tiles under 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF and so on). The gear's page and the Tools page are two clearly different places.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: OK, fair: the gear is settings and the Tools tab is tools, two clearly different pages, and the Settings page names itself. The spanner on the gear still made me hesitate at first glance, but pressing it once settled it and I wouldn't mix them up again. My complaint doesn't hold.

screen1-a3.where: Row of pill buttons under the 'PDF Reader' title: the first (left) one, 'PDF'.
screen1-a3.expectation: Switches the list below to show only my PDF files. It looks like it's already the chosen one.
screen1-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' in a pill, in a row of other file types; the chosen one is filled in with colour.

first_pass.why: Short, clear words in a neat row; the coloured one shows which is on. Easy to scan in one glance.

screen1-a4.where: Row of pill buttons under the 'PDF Reader' title: the second one, 'HWP'.
screen1-a4.expectation: Shows only my HWP files in the list below. I don't actually know what an HWP file is, but it's clearly a file type.
screen1-a4.cue: It sits in a row with PDF, Word, Excel and PPT, which are all file types, so HWP must be one too.

screen1-a8.where: Just under the file type row, on the far left of the grey 'Set as default reader' strip: a tiny faint grey X and a small book picture inside one box.
screen1-a8.expectation: I think it closes (gets rid of) the 'Set as default reader' strip. But the box is mostly around the book picture, so it might open something about the reader instead.
screen1-a8.cue: A very small, very pale X in the top-left corner of the box. The book picture next to it looks like a logo, not a button.

first_pass.why: The X is so tiny and faint I nearly missed it, and it's squashed together with a book picture that looks like decoration. I can't tell if tapping the box closes the strip or opens something. I really want this strip gone - it's an interruption - so I need the close to be obvious.
first_pass.solution: A clear, normal-sized X (or 'Not now') at the right end of the strip, separate from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the tiny pale x at the far left of the grey 'Set as default reader' strip. For a few seconds nothing seemed to happen, and I nearly pressed again. screen1-a8.closing_comment: It does exactly what I hoped: the strip goes away and nothing else happens. So what it's for is fine. The problem left is that the x is tiny, pale and slow to respond. I nearly missed it, and I nearly pressed twice because nothing happened for a few seconds. That's more about size and faintness than purpose, but it still slowed me down.

screen1-a9.where: On the right end of the grey 'Set as default reader' strip, a coloured pill button 'SET'.
screen1-a9.expectation: Makes this app my phone's default for opening documents.

first_pass.why: The strip says what it's for and the button finishes the sentence. Quick to get.

screen1-a10.where: In the middle of the screen, under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.', a big black button 'Allow Access'.

screen1-a10.cue: The button words 'Allow Access' and the sentence right above it.

first_pass.why: Big, bold, the only real thing to do on the screen, and the sentence above explains why. This is how I like it - one clear next step.

screen1-a11.where: Bottom right, just above the bottom bar: a round black button with four corner brackets in it, like a camera viewfinder.
screen1-a11.expectation: Opens the camera to scan something - probably scanning a paper document into a PDF, but it could be a QR code scanner.
screen1-a11.cue: The corner-bracket picture, which I know from scanning apps. No word on it.

first_pass.why: It's the biggest, boldest button on the page, so it's clearly important, but it has no word. Corner brackets mean both 'scan a document' and 'scan a QR code' in the apps I use, and I don't know which this is until I tap it.
first_pass.solution: Put a word on it - 'Scan' or 'Scan document' - it's the main button, it deserves a label.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the round black button with the corner marks, bottom right. After a few seconds the screen dimmed and a white box came up: 'Request permission to access all files. To read and edit your document files, please allow PDF Reader, PDF Viewer to access all your files.' It had one button, 'GO TO SET'. Nothing about scanning, no camera, and nothing telling me what the button itself would do. It's the same box every other thing throws at me. I did not press GO TO SET. I closed the box with the phone's Back key and was back on the main page. I still don't know if it's a document scanner or a QR scanner.

screen1-a11.closing_comment: Worse than I thought. Pressing the big main button didn't show me anything about what it does, just the same 'access all files' box as everything else. I still can't tell if it scans documents or QR codes, and the only way to find out is to hand over permission to all my files first. The biggest button on the screen needs a word on it: 'Scan document'.

first_pass.why: Same crown every time and I have now seen where it leads. Still the loudest thing in the corner, but I know what it is.

screen10-a2.where: Top right corner, the second little picture, next to the crown: a gear with a spanner across it.
screen10-a2.cue: The gear shape; and I have now seen a Settings page with a back arrow, and I assume this is how you get there - but the spanner still says 'tools' to me and there is a Tools tab too.

first_pass.why: I think I know it's settings by now, but only because I have seen the Settings page; the picture itself still reads as 'tools' and competes with the Tools tab at the bottom.
first_pass.solution: Either a plain gear, or a one-word label 'Settings' under it, so it can't be mixed up with the Tools tab.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a2, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the gear-with-spanner in the top right. Nothing happened for a few seconds, then a page opened with 'Settings' as its title and a back arrow. It held the same rows I'd seen before: Upgrade to Premium, Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader, Add widget, Rate App, Share App, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use. No tools at all. I pressed Back and was on the main page again. Then I pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. After a short delay it opened a totally different page of tiles under 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF and so on). The gear's page and the Tools page are two clearly different places.

screen10-a2.closing_comment: OK, fair: the gear is settings and the Tools tab is tools, two clearly different pages, and the Settings page names itself. The spanner on the gear still made me hesitate at first glance, but pressing it once settled it and I wouldn't mix them up again. My complaint doesn't hold.

screen10-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' in a pill, in a row of other file types; the chosen one is filled in with colour.

screen10-a4.where: Row of pill buttons under the 'PDF Reader' title: the second one, 'HWP'.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens

screen10-a10.where: In the middle of the screen, under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.', a big black button 'Allow Access'.

screen10-a11.where: Bottom right, just above the bottom bar: a round black button with four corner brackets in it, like a camera viewfinder.
screen10-a11.expectation: Opens the camera to scan something - probably scanning a paper document into a PDF, but it could be a QR code scanner.
screen10-a11.cue: The corner-bracket picture, which I know from scanning apps. No word on it.

first_pass.why: It's the biggest, boldest button on the page, so it's clearly important, but it has no word. Corner brackets mean both 'scan a document' and 'scan a QR code' in the apps I use, and I don't know which this is until I tap it.
first_pass.solution: Put a word on it - 'Scan' or 'Scan document' - it's the main button, it deserves a label.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a11, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the round black button with the corner marks, bottom right. After a few seconds the screen dimmed and a white box came up: 'Request permission to access all files. To read and edit your document files, please allow PDF Reader, PDF Viewer to access all your files.' It had one button, 'GO TO SET'. Nothing about scanning, no camera, and nothing telling me what the button itself would do. It's the same box every other thing throws at me. I did not press GO TO SET. I closed the box with the phone's Back key and was back on the main page. I still don't know if it's a document scanner or a QR scanner.

screen10-a11.closing_comment: Worse than I thought. Pressing the big main button didn't show me anything about what it does, just the same 'access all files' box as everything else. I still can't tell if it scans documents or QR codes, and the only way to find out is to hand over permission to all my files first. The biggest button on the screen needs a word on it: 'Scan document'.
